notes: Searched for LLM benchmarks targeting 3 underrepresented moral psychology theories: Dual Process Theory, Social Intuitionism, and Dyadic Morality. 12 queries across 4 query sets. Cross-referenced against 2,099 vault papers.

results.title: The Moral Turing Test: Evaluating Human-LLM Alignment in Moral Decision-Making
results.abstract_snippet: Creates a large corpus of human- and LLM-generated responses to moral scenarios. Finds misalignment: LLMs more sensitive to personal framing in utilitarian dilemmas. Human evaluators preferred LLM moral reasoning quality but showed anti-AI bias when source was revealed.
results.relevance_notes: Directly tests dual-process predictions (personal vs impersonal framing of trolley-type dilemmas) in LLMs. Benchmark dataset with human judgments paired.

results.title: The Greatest Good Benchmark: Measuring LLMs' Alignment with Utilitarian Moral Dilemmas
results.authors: Marraffini, Cotton, Hsueh, Fridman, Wisznia, del Corro
results.abstract_snippet: Benchmark of utilitarian moral dilemmas tested across 15 LLMs. Reveals consistently encoded moral preferences diverging from established moral theories. LLMs show preference for impartial beneficence and rejection of instrumental harm.
results.relevance_notes: Directly operationalizes the utilitarian side of Greene's dual-process framework. Benchmark dataset with systematic evaluation of utilitarian vs deontological alignment across models.

results.title: Large language models show amplified cognitive biases in moral decision-making
results.venue: PNAS (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences)
results.abstract_snippet: LLMs exhibit stronger omission bias than humans in moral dilemmas. Shows yes-no bias where LLMs flip decisions based on wording. In collective action problems, LLMs were more altruistic. Fine-tuning may amplify omission bias.
results.relevance_notes: Tests dual-process predictions (omission bias = deontological default). Omission bias amplification in LLMs is a direct test of Greene's automatic emotional response pathway. High-impact venue (PNAS).

results.title: A spiking neuron model of moral judgment in trolley dilemmas
results.abstract_snippet: MERDJ model pairs myopic automatic process with analytic system in spiking neurons to replicate deontological and utilitarian responses to trolley dilemmas. Implements Greene's dual-process framework computationally.
results.relevance_notes: Computational dual-process model but uses spiking neural networks, not LLM evaluation. Relevant as theoretical grounding but not an LLM benchmark per se.

results.title: Understanding Moral Reasoning Trajectories in Large Language Models: Toward Probing-Based Explainability
results.abstract_snippet: Introduces moral reasoning trajectories — sequences of ethical framework invocations across intermediate reasoning steps. 55-58% of consecutive steps involve framework switches. Probing-based approach localizes framework-specific encoding to specific model layers.
results.relevance_notes: Probes how LLMs switch between deontological and utilitarian frameworks during reasoning — directly tests dual-process dynamics at the representation level. Novel probing methodology.

results.title: Structured Moral Reasoning in Language Models: A Value-Grounded Evaluation Framework
results.abstract_snippet: Benchmarks 12 open-source models across 4 moral datasets using prompts grounded in value systems, ethical theories, and cognitive reasoning strategies. First-principles reasoning and Schwartz's + care-ethics scaffolds yield strongest gains.
results.relevance_notes: Tests cognitive reasoning strategies (including dual-process-inspired step-by-step decomposition) and their effect on moral reasoning quality. Includes care ethics and contractualism scaffolds. Evaluation framework paper.

results.title: LLM ethics benchmark: a three-dimensional assessment system for evaluating moral reasoning in large language models
results.abstract_snippet: Framework evaluates moral reasoning through 3 dimensions: foundational moral principles, reasoning robustness, and value consistency. Claude achieves 91.2% alignment with human moral intuitions; LLaMA shows 76.3%.
results.relevance_notes: General LLM ethics benchmark. Tests MFT alignment but does not specifically target dual process, social intuitionism, or dyadic morality frameworks. Useful reference but not theory-specific.

results.title: MoralBench: Moral Evaluation of LLMs
results.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive benchmark for probing moral dimensions of LLM outputs across ethical dilemmas reflecting real-world complexities. Develops metrics for assessing moral identity of LLMs.
results.relevance_notes: Already in vault. General moral evaluation benchmark, not specifically targeting the 3 underrepresented theories.

results.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
results.abstract_snippet: Distinguishes moral performance from moral competence. Identifies 3 challenges: facsimile problem (imitation without understanding), moral multidimensionality, moral pluralism. Argues traditional human moral cognition experiments (including dumbfounding) are less suitable for LLMs.
results.relevance_notes: High-impact Nature paper. Explicitly discusses moral dumbfounding and dual-process experiments as inadequate for LLM evaluation. Proposes new competence-based evaluation paradigm. Essential reference for the meta-evaluation project.

results.title: MoReBench: Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
results.abstract_snippet: 1,000 moral scenarios with 23,018 human-written rubric criteria. MoReBench-Theory tests 5 moral frameworks (Kantian Deontology, Benthamite Utilitarianism, Aristotelian Virtue Ethics, Scanlonian Contractualism, Gauthierian Contractarianism). 50+ PhD annotators.
results.relevance_notes: Tests dual-process-adjacent frameworks (deontology vs utilitarianism) with procedural evaluation. Extremely high annotation quality (50+ PhDs). Does not directly test intuitionism or dyadic morality.

results.title: The Pluralistic Moral Gap: Understanding Judgment and Value Differences between Humans and Large Language Models
results.abstract_snippet: Moral Dilemma Dataset of 1,618 real-world dilemmas with human judgments. 60-value taxonomy from 3,783 value expressions. LLMs rely on narrower set of moral values than humans. Dynamic Moral Profiling improves alignment by 64.3%.
results.relevance_notes: Large-scale moral dilemma dataset with value taxonomy. Relevant to intuitionism (tests whether LLMs capture the diversity of human moral intuitions) but not specifically designed as a social intuitionism benchmark.

results.title: Beyond Verdicts: Evaluating Language Model Moral Competence
results.abstract_snippet: Survey of 69 papers evaluating LLM ethical competence (2020-2025). Develops taxonomy of evaluation datasets, behaviors, metrics. Identifies overreliance on curated scenarios, overemphasis on verdict accuracy, problematic ground truth assumptions.
results.relevance_notes: Meta-survey of 69 LLM moral evaluation papers. Essential for understanding the landscape. Explicitly critiques lack of moral sensitivity testing (relevant to intuitionism's emphasis on immediate perception).

results.title: Large Language Models meet moral values: A comprehensive assessment of moral abilities
results.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
results.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive assessment using unsupervised moral classification. GPT-4 achieves superior performance. LLM responses emphasize harm/care and fairness/reciprocity but under-represent loyalty, authority, and purity.
results.relevance_notes: General MFT-based assessment. The harm/care emphasis finding is tangentially relevant to dyadic morality (harm perception) but not designed as a dyadic morality benchmark.

results.title: Revisiting the Trolley Problem for AI: Biases and Stereotypes in Large Language Models
results.abstract_snippet: Tests LLMs on trolley problem variations to examine biases and stereotypes in moral decision-making.
results.relevance_notes: Already in vault. Directly tests dual-process trolley paradigm in LLMs.

results.title: Rethinking Machine Ethics — Can LLMs Perform Moral Reasoning through the Lens of Moral Theories?
results.abstract_snippet: Tests whether LLMs can perform moral reasoning through the lens of established moral theories including deontological and utilitarian frameworks.
results.relevance_notes: Tests moral theory application in LLMs. Relevant to dual-process (deontology vs utilitarianism) but more of a general moral reasoning evaluation than a specific dual-process benchmark.

results.title: AI Psychometrics: Assessing the Psychological Profiles of Large Language Models Through Psychometric Inventories
results.abstract_snippet: Applies psychometric methodologies to evaluate psychological traits of AI systems. Reviews instruments including MFQ, MFQ-2, MFVs, MFD for moral foundations and DIT for Kohlberg's moral development stages.
results.relevance_notes: Key survey of psychometric instruments applied to LLMs. Discusses DIT (Kohlberg) and MFT instruments. Relevant methodology reference for applying moral psychology instruments to LLMs, though not a dedicated benchmark for the 3 target theories.

results.title: Human Realignment: An Empirical Study
results.abstract_snippet: Empirical study finding GPT is substantially more utilitarian than human subjects on the same moral dilemma stimulus material.
results.relevance_notes: Empirical finding on utilitarian bias in GPT. Relevant to dual-process theory (utilitarian = System 2 deliberative) but a discussion paper, not a benchmark dataset.

results.title: The Staircase of Ethics: Probing LLM Value Priorities through Multi-Step Induction to Complex Moral Dilemmas
results.abstract_snippet: Multi-step moral dilemma framework requiring models to update moral value priors across sequential stages. Tests how value priorities shift under escalating complexity.
results.relevance_notes: Multi-step moral dilemmas probe dual-process dynamics: how deliberative reasoning overrides initial intuitions under increasing complexity. Novel sequential evaluation paradigm.

results.title: A Dyadic Conversation Dataset on Moral Emotions
results.abstract_snippet: First dataset focused on moral emotions (guilt, shame, pride, compassion) in dyadic conversations. 42 participants, 14 nationalities, audio-visual cues recorded.
results.relevance_notes: Contains 'dyadic' in name but refers to dyadic conversations, not dyadic morality theory (Gray & Schein). Multimodal emotion dataset, not an LLM benchmark. Only tangentially relevant.

results.title: A survey on moral foundation theory and pre-trained language models: current advances and challenges
results.abstract_snippet: Comprehensive review of MFT-informed PLMs. Discusses care/harm dyad (relevant to dyadic morality). Reviews MFTC, MFQ, and other instruments for moral foundations detection.
results.relevance_notes: MFT survey. The care/harm foundation overlaps with dyadic morality but this is an MFT paper, not a dyadic morality benchmark.

results.title: Normative Evaluation of Large Language Models with Everyday Moral Dilemmas
results.venue: FAccT 2025 (ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency)
results.abstract_snippet: Evaluates LLMs using everyday moral dilemmas with normative framework analysis. Tests how models reason about real-world moral situations.
results.relevance_notes: FAccT paper on everyday moral dilemmas. Relevant to intuitionism (everyday moral intuitions rather than philosopher-constructed dilemmas). Not specifically targeting the 3 underrepresented theories.

results.title: Mapping Moral Reasoning in LLMs: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Safety
results.venue: AIES 2025 (AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society)
results.abstract_snippet: Multi-dimensional analysis of moral reasoning in LLMs from a safety perspective.
results.relevance_notes: Safety-focused moral reasoning analysis. General framework, not specifically targeting dual process, intuitionism, or dyadic morality.

results.title: Exploring the psychology of LLMs' moral and legal reasoning
results.abstract_snippet: Explores the psychological underpinnings of LLMs' moral and legal reasoning processes.
results.relevance_notes: Applies psychological theory to understand LLM moral reasoning. Potentially includes dual-process analysis. In a top-tier AI journal.

results.title: Robustness of large language models in moral judgements
results.abstract_snippet: Tests robustness of LLM moral judgments to minor prompt alterations. Replacing 'Case 1/Case 2' with '(A)/(B)' changes model decisions, often leading to opposite results.
results.relevance_notes: Tests stability of moral judgments under perturbation. Relevant to dual-process (shallow framing effects suggesting System-1-like processing) but not a dedicated dual-process benchmark.

results.title: Evaluating Moral Beliefs across LLMs through a Pluralistic Framework
results.abstract_snippet: Evaluates moral beliefs across LLMs using a pluralistic framework that accounts for multiple ethical perspectives.
results.relevance_notes: Pluralistic moral beliefs evaluation. General framework, not specifically targeting the 3 underrepresented theories.

results.title: AI language model rivals expert ethicist in perceived moral expertise
results.abstract_snippet: Americans rated GPT-4o ethical advice as slightly more moral, trustworthy, thoughtful, and correct than The Ethicist advice column. GPT models perceived as surpassing humans in moral justifications.
results.relevance_notes: Tests perceived moral expertise — tangentially relevant to intuitionism (quality of moral reasoning vs intuitive judgment). Not a benchmark dataset.

results.title: Diverse Human Value Alignment for Large Language Models via Ethical Reasoning
results.abstract_snippet: Diverse value alignment approach using ethical reasoning frameworks for LLMs.
results.relevance_notes: Value alignment paper, not a specific benchmark for the target theories.

results.title: Quantifying AI Psychology: A Psychometrics Benchmark for Large Language Models
results.abstract_snippet: Psychometrics benchmark for LLMs that applies psychological measurement tools to evaluate AI systems.
results.relevance_notes: Psychometric benchmark applying validated psychological instruments to LLMs. Likely includes moral psychology instruments. Relevant methodology for applying the 3 target theories.

results.title: Situational factors shape moral judgments in the trolley dilemma in Eastern, Southern, and Western countries in a culturally diverse sample
results.abstract_snippet: Cross-cultural study of trolley dilemma moral judgments examining dual-process predictions across Eastern, Southern, and Western countries.
results.vault_file: 2022-Bago-Situational factors shape moral judgments in the.md
results.relevance_notes: Already in vault. Dual-process trolley paradigm cross-cultural study. Human behavioral data, not LLM evaluation.

results.title: Probing the Moral Development of Large Language Models through Defining Issues Test
results.abstract_snippet: Applies Kohlberg's Defining Issues Test to probe moral development stages in LLMs.
results.vault_file: 2023-Deng-Probing the Moral Development of Large Language.md
results.relevance_notes: Already in vault. Uses DIT (Kohlberg), not directly testing the 3 underrepresented theories.

results.title: Evaluating the Moral Beliefs Encoded in LLMs
results.abstract_snippet: Evaluates moral beliefs encoded in LLMs using systematic probing of ethical stances.
results.vault_file: 2023-Scherrer-Evaluating the Moral Beliefs Encoded in LLMs.md
results.relevance_notes: Already in vault. General moral beliefs evaluation.

key_findings.dual_process_coverage: Best represented of the 3 target theories. Multiple papers test utilitarian-vs-deontological framing in LLMs (Greatest Good Benchmark, Moral Turing Test, PNAS cognitive biases paper). The Moral Reasoning Trajectories paper (2026) probes dual-process dynamics at the representation level. However, none explicitly frame their work as 'dual process theory evaluation' — they use trolley/utilitarian paradigms without citing Greene's dual-process model as the theoretical basis.
key_findings.intuitionist_coverage: NEAR ZERO dedicated benchmarks found. No paper specifically tests Haidt's social intuitionist model predictions (intuition-first, post-hoc rationalization, social persuasion) in LLMs. The Gabriel et al. Nature roadmap (2026) explicitly notes that moral dumbfounding experiments are unsuitable for LLMs. The Pluralistic Moral Gap paper tests value diversity (tangentially related) but not the intuitionist mechanism.
key_findings.dyadic_coverage: ZERO dedicated benchmarks found. No paper specifically tests Gray & Schein's dyadic morality predictions (agent-patient typecasting, harm perception as the core of moral judgment) in LLMs. The MFT care/harm dimension overlaps conceptually but no benchmark operationalizes dyadic morality theory specifically.
key_findings.recommendation: The gap is confirmed and severe for Social Intuitionism and Dyadic Morality. For Dual Process Theory, there are implicit tests (trolley paradigms) but no benchmark that explicitly operationalizes Greene's framework. The 14 not_in_vault_relevant papers should be considered for vault addition regardless, as they strengthen the moral psychology benchmark coverage. Top priority additions: (1) Gabriel et al. 2026 Nature roadmap, (2) Cheung et al. 2025 PNAS cognitive biases, (3) Greatest Good Benchmark (EMNLP 2024), (4) MoReBench (50+ PhD annotators), (5) Moral Reasoning Trajectories (2026).
